examples.en: Autumn rain fell and the weather turned chilly.
Today the picnic was canceled because of the autumn rain.
I drank tea while watching the autumn rain outside the window.
The road is full of leaves wet from the autumn rain.
For autumn rain, it came down quite a lot.

examples.ko: 가을비 오는 날에는 따뜻한 국물이 생각나요.
examples.en: On autumn rainy days I crave something with warm broth.

explain: '봄비, 가을비, 겨울비'처럼 계절 이름에 '비'를 붙여 그 계절에 오는 비를 말해요. 발음은 쓴 대로 [가을비]예요. 가을비가 한 번 오면 날씨가 쌀쌀해졌다고 느끼는 경우가 많아서, 가을비 뒤에 겉옷을 챙기라는 말을 자주 해요.
explain_en: Like '봄비', '가을비' and '겨울비', you add '비' to a season name to mean rain of that season. It is pronounced as written, [가을비]. After autumn rain the air often feels noticeably cooler, so people may tell you to bring a jacket.

examples.en: I borrowed an interesting science book from the library.
The science book has many pictures, so it's easy to understand.
My younger sibling likes reading science books.
The science book was more fun than I expected, which surprised me.
The science books are in the children's section of the bookstore.

examples.ko: 이번 달에는 과학책도 몇 권 샀어요.
examples.en: This month I bought a few science books too.

explain: '소설책, 동화책, 만화책'처럼 내용에 따라 책 종류를 말할 때 써요. 어린이가 읽는 과학 이야기 책을 떠올릴 때 특히 자연스러워요. 책을 세는 말은 '권'이에요.
explain_en: It is used like '소설책', '동화책' and '만화책' to name a type of book by its content. It sounds especially natural for science storybooks that children read. The counter for books is '권'.

examples.en: When the yellow light comes on, I slow down.
The traffic light turned yellow while I was crossing.
It's dangerous to just drive through when the light is yellow.
Don't rush across when the light is yellow.
The car in front suddenly stopped at the yellow light.
There's a traffic light where only the yellow keeps blinking.

explain: 신호등은 빨간불, 노란불, 초록불 순서로 말해요. 초록불은 '파란불'이라고 부르는 사람도 많아요. 노란불에는 멈출 준비를 하라는 신호예요.
explain_en: Traffic lights are named 빨간불, 노란불 and 초록불. Many people call the green light '파란불' too. The yellow light is a signal to get ready to stop.

en: to become hot; to grow warm

examples.en: If the pot gets too hot, turn down the heat.
Wait until the frying pan gets hot.
When I turned on the heater, the room got hot quickly.
The soup had cooled, so I reheated it and it got hot.
When it's midday, the sand gets too hot.

examples.ko: 햇볕에 있었더니 팔이 뜨거워지는 것 같아요.
examples.en: After being in the sun, my arms feel like they are heating up.

explain: '뜨겁다'는 손이나 몸에 닿는 열이 셀 때 써서, 날씨가 더울 때 쓰는 '더워지다'와 달라요. '따뜻해지다'는 기분 좋게 따뜻한 정도이고, 반대말은 '차가워지다'나 '식다'예요. 'ㅂ' 불규칙이라 '뜨거워요, 뜨거워져요'로 바뀌어요.

phrases.en: I remembered my mistake and my face burned with embarrassment.
phrases.nuance_ko: 실제로 열이 나는 게 아니라 창피하거나 부끄러울 때 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: It does not mean a real fever; it is used when you feel embarrassed or ashamed.

explain_en: '뜨겁다' is about heat you feel by touch, unlike '더워지다', which is for hot weather. '따뜻해지다' is a pleasant warmth, and the opposites are '차가워지다' or '식다'. It is a ㅂ-irregular word, so it becomes '뜨거워요' and '뜨거워져요'.

examples.en: I wiped the baby's hands with a wet tissue.
I always carry wet wipes in my bag.

examples.ko: 물티슈 한 장만 줄 수 있어요?
examples.en: Could you give me just one wet wipe?
You must not flush wet wipes down the toilet.

examples.ko: 물티슈가 다 말라서 새 걸 샀어요.
examples.en: The wet wipes dried out, so I bought new ones.

examples.ko: 물티슈 포장지에 사용 방법이 쓰여 있어요.
examples.en: The usage instructions are written on the wet wipes package.

explain: 마른 휴지는 '휴지'나 '티슈', 젖은 휴지는 '물티슈'라고 해서 구분해요. '한 장, 두 장'으로 세요. 한국 식당에서는 손을 닦으라고 물티슈를 자주 줘요.
explain_en: Dry paper is 휴지 or 티슈, and the damp kind is 물티슈, so they are kept apart. Count them as 한 장, 두 장. Korean restaurants often hand out 물티슈 for your hands.

examples.en: I hear footsteps from upstairs late at night.
The child tiptoed along, muffling the sound of his steps.
I can tell it's Dad just from the footsteps.

examples.ko: 누가 오는지 발소리로 알 수 있어요.
examples.en: I can tell who is coming by the footsteps.
The footsteps woke me up.
The upstairs neighbor's footsteps sound really loud.

explain: '발소리가 나다/들리다', '발소리를 죽이다'처럼 자주 써요. '발자국 소리'도 같은 뜻으로 쓰고, '발자국'만 말하면 땅에 남은 자국이에요. 아파트에서는 층간 소음 이야기에서 많이 나와요.
explain_en: Common patterns are '발소리가 나다/들리다' and '발소리를 죽이다'. '발자국 소리' means the same, but '발자국' alone is the mark left on the ground. It often comes up in talk about noise between apartment floors.

examples.en: One glass of ice water here, please.
After exercising, I gulped down ice water.

examples.ko: 얼음물에 손을 담그니 정신이 번쩍 들어요.
examples.en: Dipping my hand in ice water makes me snap awake.

examples.ko: 더운 날에는 얼음물을 보온병에 담아 다녀요.
examples.en: On hot days, I carry ice water in a thermos.
Ice water is so cold that it hurts my teeth.
I soaked a towel in ice water and put it on my forehead.

explain: '찬물'은 그냥 차가운 물이고, '얼음물'은 얼음이 들어 있는 물이에요. 식당에서는 차가운 물을 '냉수'라고 부르는 곳도 있어요. 따뜻한 물은 '따뜻한 물'이나 '온수'라고 해요.
explain_en: '찬물' is simply cold water, while '얼음물' has ice in it. Some restaurants call cold water '냉수'. Warm water is '따뜻한 물' or '온수'.

examples.ko: 시험 전날에는 잡생각이 많아서 잠이 안 와요.
examples.en: The night before an exam, I have so many stray thoughts that I can't sleep.
After exercising, the stray thoughts disappear.

examples.ko: 공부할 때 잡생각 때문에 집중이 안 돼요.
examples.en: When I study, I can't focus because of wandering thoughts.
I listen to music to get rid of distracting thoughts.

examples.ko: 쓸데없는 잡생각 좀 그만하고 일찍 자요.
examples.en: Stop the pointless thinking and go to bed early.
I got lost in random thoughts while walking and passed my stop.

explain: '잡생각이 들다/나다/많다'처럼 쓰고, 없앨 때는 '잡생각을 버리다'라고 해요. 일이나 공부에 집중하지 못하게 하는 쓸데없는 생각이라서 조금 부정적이에요. 비슷한 말로 '잡념'이 있는데 글에서 더 많이 보여요.
explain_en: Say '잡생각이 들다/나다/많다', and '잡생각을 버리다' to get rid of them. It's a bit negative, since these are useless thoughts that stop you from focusing on work or study. A similar word is '잡념', which you see more in writing.

examples.ko: 우리 반에 전학생이 한 명 왔어요.
examples.en: A transfer student joined our class.

examples.ko: 전학생은 아직 친구가 없어서 외로워 보여요.
examples.en: The transfer student has no friends yet and looks lonely.
I was a transfer student when I was little too.

examples.ko: 선생님이 반 친구들에게 전학생을 소개해 주셨어요.
examples.en: The teacher introduced the transfer student.

examples.ko: 전학생이 와서 반 분위기가 조금 달라졌어요.
examples.en: With the transfer student here, the class mood changed a little.

examples.ko: 전학생 옆자리에 앉은 친구가 학교를 안내했어요.
examples.en: The friend sitting next to the transfer student showed them around the school.

explain: 학교를 옮기는 일은 '전학하다', '전학 오다', '전학 가다'로 말해요. 반만 바꾸는 것은 전학이 아니에요. 대학에서 다른 학교로 옮기는 것은 '편입'이라고 해요.
explain_en: Moving schools is '전학하다', '전학 오다' or '전학 가다'. Changing only your class is not 전학. At the university level, moving to another school is called 편입.

examples.en: The room was so cold that I turned on the heater.
This car's heater warms up quickly.

examples.ko: 사무실 히터는 오후 여섯 시에 꺼져요.
examples.en: The office heater turns off at six in the evening.
I got sleepy on the bus because of the heater.

examples.ko: 히터에 손을 대면 데일 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can get burned if you touch the heater.
The heater air was hot, so I lowered the temperature.

explain: 집 전체를 데우는 바닥 난방과 달리, 히터는 한 곳을 따뜻하게 하는 기계예요. 차에서는 '히터를 틀다', 방에서는 '히터를 켜다'라고 많이 해요. 반대로 시원하게 하는 기계는 에어컨이에요.
explain_en: Unlike floor heating that warms a whole home, a 히터 warms one spot. People say '히터를 틀다' for a car and '히터를 켜다' for a room. The machine that cools instead is the 에어컨.
